hard: The scan is cropped at the right edge: lines to the right of FE 14 and the strainer leave the image and are not edges; LIC 41 is cut by the edge.

Flow elements FE 14 (magnetic, M box), FE 15, FE 16 (bowtie with bars), the flexible hoses, reducers and the hatched flow conditioner are keyed as class general (in-line elements); the small square on the left loop (sq_left) is keyed general with unknown meaning.

Leader lines from hand-valve tag bubbles (HV 1/2/6/7) and FE bubbles to their elements are keyed as edges of kind i, because PID2Graph-style keys join drawn lines; a reader that does not report leader lines loses those connections.
LV 41 bubble has no line to the LV 41 valve body; only its dashed line to LC 41 is keyed.
The dashed line from TC 42 meets the HMS 91 / TT 42 vertical at one point (junction j_hms).

uncertain.why: a short solid line leaves LAHH 91 toward LSH 91 with a visible gap; read as a link
whether HMS 91 is joined to the TC 42 - TT 42 dashed line or the line only passes under it
small square on the left loop below HV 6: function unknown (keyed general)
bowtie-with-bars symbols tagged FE: flow element vs valve

consistency_check.method: same agent re-keyed, from fresh crops and without opening the key, every symbol whose centre lies in a seeded random 20% of a 5 x 4 cell grid (seed 20261029) and the links between those symbols; compared at IoU >= 0.5 with class. NOT independent: the same agent made the key and still had it in context.

hard: A second scan of the SAME drawing as Sch_ma_P_ID (not independent data). Its key is the Sch_ma_P_ID key moved by an affine map fitted on the 19 instrument bubbles both scans share (Hough circle centres): residual max 3.9 px, mean 1.5 px; the overlay was checked by eye on the whole sheet. Every ambiguity of Sch_ma_P_ID carries over.

consistency_check.method: not re-keyed: this key is the Sch_ma_P_ID key transferred by an affine fit (see hard); its consistency is that of Sch_ma_P_ID plus the fit residual

hard: SC01 and SC02 are keyed as class 'general' (heat exchangers): SC01 is fed with Vapore vivo and returns condensate (the crystallizer heater); SC02 takes the SP01 vapour and cooling water (condenser). The caller's brief listed them as vessels; the class table puts heat exchangers under general. SP01 (separator/crystallizer body) is tank.

SC01 box spans the whole drawn exchanger stack from the top head flange (y~604) to the bottom A nozzle (y~1070), not just the rectangle labelled 'SC 01' (y 705-800); nozzles E, D, L, L, T, Q, P attach to it.
The small 'flag on a stub' symbols (13) are keyed as inlet/outlet line ends (vent/sample connections); their exact meaning is not certain.

Not keyed: small 'RI00'/'R100' text boxes next to TT bubbles, the 'A' lozenge (SP01 tangential inlet nozzle), triangular wall marks on SC01/SC02, blind-flanged nozzles, the wavy hose sections at SP01 S/R, impulse tap stubs on FE05/FE06/FE07.
Downcomer (250-Pra-008-HC) branch nozzles are modelled as junctions on the pipe (j_dc728 ... j_dc1037).
TE bubbles (TE01-TE05, TE07) sit beside the TT tappings with no drawn line; keyed as instruments without edges.
Purge/bubbler lines (pW -> FI rotameters -> LT01 / DT01 impulse lines) are keyed as kind i; the in-line rotameter FI04 on the 25-Wr-013 cooling-water line is keyed with kind p.
The SC02 bottom drain (line joining nozzles B and A at y~515 to a small vertical symbol at x~1706) is read as a drain valve; uncertain.
Bubble digits are about 4 px tall in this JPEG; many tag numbers are read from blocky glyphs.
